seo.title: DOM Battlefield: a squad tactics tank game in your browser
seo.description: Command up to twelve tanks: freeze time to plan every route, then radio your squad through the firefight. Free tank tactics in your browser.

sections.heading: DOM Battlefield
sections.headingAccent: Squad tactics in a browser tab.
sections.body: Command a platoon of up to twelve tanks on a grid built from real page elements. Pick the ground, freeze time to plan every route, then radio your squad through a live firefight. Free in your browser: no install, no account.

image.alt: DOM Battlefield mid-battle: the green platoon pushes across the grid toward HQ B while pink tanks hold the cover, with the sector map in the corner

items.title: Pick the ground
items.body: Choose one of four operations, a terrain density and your side, or press Quick start and anything you have not picked is rolled at random.

items.title: Plan the battle
items.body: Time is frozen. Set your formation and a squad of 4, 8 or 12 tanks. Fill a four-slot scout, medium and heavy loadout within 12 points, then give each tank an order.

items.title: Fight
items.body: Press Start battle. Drive your command tank with WASD or the arrows, aim with the pointer and hold Space or click to fire. Your command tank must survive.

items.title: Command under fire
items.body: Press O for Command mode: time runs at half speed and your gun is off while you send tanks to new squares. F, R and E order fall in, retreat and advance.

items.title: Win
items.body: Capture the enemy HQ, hold the contested crossroads, or eliminate their platoon.

items.title: Drive
items.body: WASD or the arrow keys. On phones, the analog thumbstick.

items.title: Aim and fire
items.body: Aim with the pointer; hold Space, click or right-click to fire. On phones, aim goes to the nearest visible enemy: hold Fire.

items.title: Squad orders
items.body: F fall in, R retreat, E advance. On phones, the labeled buttons.

items.title: Pick a wingman
items.body: 1–9 or click a tank. On phones, tap the tank or its platoon key.

items.title: Command mode
items.body: O, then a tank and a square. Enter locks the order, Backspace clears it, N moves to the next tank and H attacks the HQ.

items.title: Pause and camera
items.body: P or the white flag pauses: Keep fighting or Surrender. M and drag pans, C recenters.

items.title: Quick start
items.body: Anything you have not picked is rolled at random, and the battle starts.

items.title: Plan battle
items.body: Time stays frozen while three cards set your platoon, your loadout and every tank's route. Start battle when you are ready.

items.title: Four operations
items.body: Hedgerow breach, Desert spearhead, Winter crossroads and Twin bridges, each with Light, Normal or Heavy terrain and a dice for a new layout.

items.title: Three ways to win
items.body: Capture an opposing HQ, hold a contested crossroads, or eliminate a platoon.

items.title: Retreat to repair
items.body: Retreat sends your squad back to headquarters, where tanks repair. Advance returns them to the objective.

items.title: Bend the route
items.body: Drag a route line or its flag to change where a tank goes. Every map has alternate connected routes.

items.title: Know your cover
items.body: Houses, hedges and parked cars break into debris and rubble. Rocks and water are permanent; fences stop tanks but let shells through.

items.title: True full screen on phones
items.body: On iPhone, Add to Home Screen; on Android, Install. The first visit on a phone explains how.

items.title: Spend the 12 points on purpose
items.body: Each loadout slot costs points: a scout 2, a medium 3, a heavy 4, and four slots must fit 12. Scouts are fastest with the quickest reload; heavies take the most damage and hit hardest but move slowest. Squads of 8 and 12 repeat the pattern, so one choice shapes the whole squad.

items.title: Play the objective, not the kill count
items.body: A capture means holding the opposing HQ for 12 seconds with no defender nearby. A crossroads must be held for 45 uncontested seconds. Elimination means breaking all four defenders. Plan routes for the one your operation asks for.

items.title: Keep your command tank alive
items.body: Your command tank must survive, whatever the objective. Let the squad take the lead into contested ground and route your own tank behind it.

items.title: Plan while time is frozen
items.body: In Plan, time stays frozen: give every tank an order and lock its route before Start battle. In battle, Command runs at half speed with your gun off, so redirect quickly and switch back to Auto or Lock.

items.title: Repair before you push
items.body: Damaged tanks lose up to 45% of their top speed. Retreat to headquarters to repair, then Advance back to the objective by a different lane: every map has alternate connected routes.

items.title: Open lanes through soft cover
items.body: Hedges and houses stop shells until they are destroyed, so blast a lane first and bring the squad through. Fences block tanks but not shells; rock ridges and water never break.

items.title: Same battles
items.body: DOM Battlefield now runs on the Fizlet engine. Gameplay is unchanged: the new step plays the 0.18.13 battles identically.

items.title: Same seed, same battle
items.body: Every random roll in play comes from the map's seed, so a map replays the same way from the same inputs.

items.title: No garbage-collection hitches
items.body: Once warm, a battle step allocates nothing (tested: no minor GC over 20,000 busy steps).

items.question: Is DOM Battlefield free to play?
items.answer: Yes. It plays in your browser with no install and no account, and it is open source (MIT).

items.question: Can I play DOM Battlefield on a phone?
items.answer: Yes. Phone battles put a see-through rail on each side of a full-screen field, with an analog thumbstick and labeled buttons.

items.question: How is it related to Sherman Bytes?
items.answer: Same tanks: Sherman Bytes draws every tank with its own sprite code. DOM Battlefield adds zero bytes to the Sherman game.

items.question: Is there a two-player mode?
items.answer: Not in DOM Battlefield yet. Battlefield Blitz, its arcade version, has a two-player mode.
